proposal_reason:
ANALYSIS: No fusion trials yet. Single models with meta are close (0.862-0.870 AUROC), and all tuned baselines prefer strong regularisation (C 1e-4 to 1e-3) with low-dim PCA or L2. Since the models are similarly strong and likely partly complementary, simple averaging of well-tuned members is the natural first probe.
REASONING: late_tuned with mean_prob has no free knobs. It uses each member at its own best setting and tests directly whether averaging three strong, possibly complementary models beats the best single model (0.870). This gives a reference point for the exploration phase.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC around 0.875-0.885, a small gain over uni2h+meta from variance reduction. If it does not beat 0.870, the models are largely redundant, and gains would have to come from learned weighting or early fusion rather than plain averaging.

ANALYSIS: Late fusion of the three tuned members with mean_prob gives 0.8792, about +0.009 over the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.8701). The gain is spread across classes; Papillary (0.78) and Lepidic (0.83) remain the weakest. Early, gated and stack variants are still untested.
REASONING: During exploration I should map each method family. early_tuned is the natural counterpart to late_tuned: it keeps each member's tuned preprocessing and learns block weights. With PCA 16+32 plus the full-dimensional H-optimus block, a small C is appropriate. I will start with C=0.001 and meta_weight=3, the middle values among the members' tuned settings.
EXPECTED: I expect roughly 0.87-0.88. If early_tuned clearly beats late_tuned mean_prob, joint fitting helps. If it falls near the single-model level, the full-dimensional H-optimus block probably dominates or overfits, and late averaging is the better direction.

ANALYSIS: Both tuned fusions beat the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870): late_tuned mean_prob reached 0.879 and early_tuned 0.876. The gains are modest, about 0.006-0.009, which is probably near the acceptance threshold. Papillary (0.76-0.78) and Lepidic (0.83) are the weakest classes. The plain early, late and gated methods have not been tested yet.
REASONING: Exploration should map the untested methods. A plain early fusion is the natural next step. It uses L2 normalisation, PCA 32 per model, balanced blocks, meta_weight 3 and strong regularisation (C=0.001), which is close to what the single models preferred. This tests whether a shared low-dimensional PCA with equal block variance matches the tuned early fusion.
EXPECTED: I expect an AUROC of about 0.870-0.878. If it is clearly lower, say below 0.865, then the per-model tuning matters and I will focus on the tuned variants and the late combiners. If it is higher, I will explore the balance_blocks, PCA and C settings of plain early fusion.

ANALYSIS: All three fusion methods tried so far land at 0.876-0.879 AUROC, about 0.006-0.009 above the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.8701). That gap is likely near the noise threshold. Papillary (~0.77) and Lepidic (~0.83) are the weakest classes in every trial. Late fusion with plain averaging is marginally best, which suggests the gain comes from diversity across models.
REASONING: Exploration should cover every method. Gated and plain late fusion are untested, and late_tuned has only been tried with one combiner. The gated network is the riskiest method, so testing it early tells us whether it is worth any further budget. I chose a strongly regularised setting because only 134 patients train each fold: PCA 32 with L2 normalisation (matching the best early config), hidden 32, dropout 0.5, weight_decay 0.1, 200 epochs, lr 0.001, 3 seeds.
EXPECTED: I expect roughly 0.86-0.875, likely below the logistic-regression fusions because the network overfits. If it reaches at least 0.88, gated deserves follow-up on hidden size and weight decay. If it falls below 0.86, I will drop gated and spend the remaining budget on late and late_tuned combiners and on early-fusion C and PCA.

ANALYSIS: All four fusion methods land at 0.876-0.879, roughly +0.006-0.009 over the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870), which is likely near or below the acceptance threshold. late_tuned mean_prob is best so far. Papillary (0.76-0.79) and Lepidic (0.81-0.84) are the weak classes across methods. The plain late method is untested.
REASONING: In exploration I should map the untested method, which is plain late fusion with shared settings. I use a stack combiner with moderate stack_C so the second-level model can learn per-class reweighting of the models, the one thing mean_prob cannot do. This could help the weak Papillary and Lepidic classes. The base settings (L2 on, PCA 32, meta_weight 3, C 0.001) match the reasonable early config in #3, so the comparison stays clean.
EXPECTED: If stacking adds value, I expect AUROC ≥0.880, with gains on Papillary and Lepidic. If it comes in below about 0.875, stacking overfits with 134 patients (inner-CV noise), and simple averaging is the better combiner. Late_tuned with mean_logit or learned_weights would then be the next thing to explore.

ANALYSIS: All five fusion methods land at 0.876-0.880, about 0.005-0.01 above the best single baseline (uni2h+meta 0.870), which is near the noise threshold. Late fusion is marginally ahead: stack 0.8795 and late_tuned mean_prob 0.8792. Gated reaches similar AUROC and higher BA but has a larger SD. Papillary (~0.77-0.79) and Lepidic (~0.83) are the weak classes everywhere.
REASONING: In the exploration phase I want to map the knobs most likely to matter. Early fusion has only been tested at C=0.001 with PCA 32. A less compressed, less regularised early config (no PCA, L2, balanced blocks, C=0.01) tests whether the PCA bottleneck is limiting the joint model. With full-dimensional, standardised features, C=0.01 is moderate. This maps an untested region of the main method instead of repeating near-duplicates of the late variants.
EXPECTED: If more dimensions help, AUROC should reach about 0.885 or higher, with gains in Papillary and Lepidic. If it drops to about 0.87 or lower, then strong compression with heavy shrinkage is the right regime, and further effort should go to late/stack combinations around PCA 16-32.

ANALYSIS: All fusion methods cluster at 0.875-0.880, roughly 0.01 above the best single model (uni2h+meta, 0.870). Late fusion leads: stack gives 0.8795 and late_tuned mean_prob gives 0.8792. Early fusion without PCA (#6) is worse, so dimensionality reduction matters. Papillary (~0.78) and Lepidic (~0.83) are the weakest classes in every method.
REASONING: The exploration phase should map the parts of the space not yet tried. Shared-config late fusion with stronger regularization (C=0.0001, close to the Virchow2 tuned setting) and PCA=16 is untested. A cheaper combine (mean_logit) avoids the inner-CV noise that stack adds. Together these test whether heavier shrinkage helps late fusion on only 134 training patients per fold.
EXPECTED: I expect about 0.878-0.885. If it comes in below 0.875, strong shrinkage plus PCA=16 is underfitting, and the next trials should stay near C=0.001 and PCA=32 and vary only the combine rule.

ANALYSIS: All fusion methods cluster at 0.875-0.880, about 0.01 above the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870). Late fusion (tuned mean_prob 0.879, stack 0.8795) is marginally ahead of early (0.877) and gated (0.876). Full-dimensional early fusion without PCA is worse (0.870), so dimensionality reduction matters. Papillary (~0.77-0.79) and Lepidic (~0.80-0.85) remain the weak classes.
REASONING: Two exploration slots remain. Untested regions that could plausibly give a clear gain are stacking on the tuned members and early fusion with a higher C. Stacking on the tuned members combines the best member settings with a learned combiner, which was the best combine in shared-config late fusion (#5). This also directly compares stack with mean_prob for the same members.
EXPECTED: Expect AUROC around 0.880-0.885 with better BA, from the stacker learning class-specific trust in each model (e.g., Papillary). If it comes in at or below 0.879, the learned combination adds no information beyond simple averaging. In that case, simple averaging of tuned members is near the ceiling, and the remaining budget should go to early fusion regularisation and PCA variants.

ANALYSIS: All fusion variants land at 0.870-0.880, about 0.005-0.01 above the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870), which is within the usual noise threshold. Late fusion with simple averaging (#1 late_tuned mean_prob 0.879) or a regularised stack (#5 0.8795) is best. Stacking on the tuned members (#8) hurt, so inner-CV stacking is fragile. Early fusion with no PCA (#6) was worse than with PCA 32, which points toward strong dimensionality reduction. The gated method gave the highest BA but more variance across folds.
REASONING: Two exploration trials remain. learned_weights on the tuned members is untested, and it tells us whether a non-uniform weighting (including picking the single best model) beats equal averaging. If it doesn't, mean_prob stays the robust default. This answers an open question cheaply before the stop rule starts.
EXPECTED: AUROC around 0.875-0.88. If it falls below mean_prob, the inner-CV weight estimates are noisy at n=134, and later trials should focus on fixed averaging: late with shared C/PCA and mean_prob, or a higher stack_C. If it clearly beats mean_prob, the models contribute unequally and weighting is worth exploring further.

ANALYSIS: All fusion methods cluster at 0.870-0.880 AUROC, about 0.005-0.01 above the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870). Simple averaging (late_tuned mean_prob 0.879, late stack 0.880) is at least as good as learned combiners. Learned weights and stacking on tuned members underperform (0.867-0.869), consistent with inner-CV noise at n=134. Papillary (~0.77-0.79) and Lepidic (~0.81-0.85) are the weak classes in every trial.
REASONING: This is the last exploration slot. One unmapped dimension is strong regularization with full features in early fusion: pca=None was tried only at C=0.01 (0.870), while the tuned members favoured very small C. Early fusion with pca=64, C=0.0001 and balance_blocks tests whether keeping more dimensions under heavier shrinkage helps. Of the remaining knobs, this one seems most likely to shift the plateau rather than re-sample it.
EXPECTED: I expect about 0.875-0.882. If it does not beat 0.879, then dimensionality and C in early fusion are not the bottleneck, and the plateau near 0.88 is the limit of these embeddings. In that case the later search should focus on plain late averaging variants (shared C and PCA with mean_prob) and on gated regularization, rather than on more early-fusion grids.
decision_reason: exploration phase: nothing is accepted; end of exploration: trial 10 (highest mean AUROC of the 10 explored trials) becomes the current best

proposal_reason:
ANALYSIS: All fusion methods land at 0.870-0.884, slightly above the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870). The best so far is trial #10: early fusion with L2 norm, PCA 64, balanced blocks and very strong shrinkage (C=1e-4), at 0.8844 with the lowest fold SD. Two patterns stand out: going from PCA 32 to 64 while lowering C from 1e-3 to 1e-4 helped, and learned or stacked combiners on the tuned members did worse, which suggests inner-CV weighting overfits at n=134.
REASONING: The open question is whether the gain came from keeping more PCA components under heavy shrinkage. PCA 128 at C=1e-4, with everything else fixed, tests that trend directly. It is a coherent extension of the winning configuration that could plausibly add a clear gain, not a tiny tweak.
EXPECTED: If the trend continues, AUROC should reach about 0.89, which might clear the acceptance threshold. If it is flat or lower, 64 components is near the optimum along this axis. In that case I would next probe C (1e-3 at PCA 64) or meta_weight, rather than component count.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion with per-slide L2, PCA per model, balanced blocks and very strong shrinkage (C=1e-4) is best (0.8844, lowest fold SD). PCA 64 and 128 are indistinguishable, so at this C the fit is dominated by the top components and dimensionality is no longer the lever. Late and gated fusion and the tuned variants all sit at 0.867-0.880.
REASONING: C is already at the bottom of its grid, so the metadata columns are being shrunk almost as hard as the image features. Age and sex carry some separate signal (0.60 AUROC alone), and H-optimus preferred meta_weight=10 as a single model. Raising meta_weight to 10 gives the metadata 100x less effective penalty while leaving the image blocks unchanged. This is a clean one-knob test of something still open.
EXPECTED: A modest gain (+0.003 to +0.008), mainly in classes linked to age or sex (In situ, Lepidic), with a stable fold SD. If it is flat or worse, metadata is already used enough at meta_weight=3. I would then move to l2_normalize=False or balance_blocks=False at the best setting, or to stacking late fusion at C=1e-4.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion with per-slide L2, balanced blocks and very strong shrinkage (C=1e-4) is best (0.8844, lowest fold SD). PCA 64 vs 128 and meta_weight 3 vs 10 made no difference, so at this C the ridge penalty, not the PCA dimension, controls complexity. The earlier no-PCA run (#6) used a much weaker C=0.01 and did worse, so it confounded PCA with C.
REASONING: The open question is whether PCA helps at all once shrinkage is strong. Running pca=None at C=1e-4 isolates that. Full-dimensional ridge keeps directions that a fold-wise PCA throws away, and it could plausibly add a clear gain. If it does not, PCA truncation can be considered settled and the remaining budget moves to other knobs: l2_normalize, balance_blocks, and C=1e-3 at pca 64.
EXPECTED: AUROC around 0.884-0.89. If it is not better than #10 beyond the threshold, I conclude that PCA dimension is irrelevant under strong shrinkage. Next I would test l2_normalize=False and balance_blocks=False at pca 64.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion is clearly best once heavily regularised: going from C=0.001 (#3, 0.8772) to C=0.0001 (#10, 0.8844) gave the only clear gain. PCA 64, 128 and none, and meta_weight 3 vs 10, all sit within noise at about 0.884-0.885. Late and gated fusion and the tuned variants top out around 0.879. Papillary (about 0.78) and Lepidic (about 0.82) remain the weak classes.
REASONING: C is already at the smallest value in the grid, and PCA and meta_weight look flat. The main untested early knob in this regime is the per-slide L2 normalisation. balance_blocks matters little at PCA 64, because every block already has the same number of columns. Turning L2 off at the best setting tells us whether the slide-norm information (which differs between attention-pooled and Prism embeddings) helps or hurts under strong shrinkage.
EXPECTED: Most likely within ±0.003 of #10, which would mean L2 is irrelevant and the early-fusion plateau is near 0.885. In that case I would stop tuning early fusion and probe late fusion with strong shared shrinkage (C=0.0001, stack or mean_prob). A clear drop would confirm that L2 matters. A gain above threshold would make L2-off the new base for nearby variants.

ANALYSIS: Strong regularisation was the main driver: early fusion with balanced blocks and C=0.0001 (#10, 0.8844) clearly beat the C=0.001-0.01 versions (0.870-0.877). Changing PCA, meta_weight or L2 at C=0.0001 (#11-#14) moved AUROC by under 0.001. Early fusion has plateaued around 0.884-0.885. Late fusion has only been tested at weaker C or with mean_logit and PCA 16.
REASONING: There is no point searching early-fusion knobs further. The open question is whether averaging three separately fitted, heavily shrunk members beats one joint model at the same shrinkage. Simple mean_prob was the best combiner in the late_tuned runs (#1 vs #8 and #9), while the learned combiners overfit. This trial reuses the winning preprocessing (L2, PCA 64, meta_weight 3, C=0.0001) so that only the fusion type changes.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of about 0.883-0.888. A clear gain would show that ensemble averaging adds diversity beyond joint fitting. If it ties or falls below #10, fusion type does not matter at strong regularisation. I would then make one or two final checks: balance_blocks=False, and a heavily regularised gated model. If neither helps, I would accept #10 as near the ceiling.

ANALYSIS: Strongly regularised early fusion (C=1e-4, L2 norm, balanced blocks) sits on a flat plateau of about 0.884–0.885. PCA 64, 128 or none, meta_weight 3 or 10 and L2 on or off all give differences within noise. Late and late_tuned combiners are clearly worse (0.867–0.880), and the only gated trial (0.876) was lightly regularised but had the best BA (0.511). Rerunning early variants is unlikely to beat the threshold.
REASONING: The early-fusion knobs look exhausted, so the remaining open question is whether a per-patient gate can add something beyond the linear model once it is regularised as heavily as the winning early model. Trial #4 used weight_decay 0.1, hidden 32 and PCA 32. A smaller projection (16), the strongest weight decay (1.0), dropout 0.5, and PCA 64 (the best early setting) test that question directly. The other settings stay matched to the best early fusion: L2 norm and meta_weight 3.
EXPECTED: If heavy regularisation is what gated was missing, AUROC should reach about 0.885–0.89 and keep its BA advantage, ideally lifting Papillary and Lepidic. If it stays near 0.875 or below, I will conclude that the gate cannot be learned from about 134 patients per fold. I would then spend only a few more trials, such as early with balance_blocks=False or early_tuned at C=1e-4, before accepting #10 as final.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion with per-slide L2, balanced blocks and the strongest shrinkage (C=1e-4) sits on a plateau at about 0.884-0.885 AUROC (#10-#14). PCA size, meta_weight and L2 all make differences of 0.001 or less there. At the same strong C, mean_prob late fusion is clearly worse (#15). Gated networks overfit (#16). The tuned-member variants did not beat simple shared settings. Stacking was the best late combiner (#5, 0.8795), but it was only tried at C=1e-3 with PCA 32.
REASONING: Knobs within early fusion now move AUROC by less than the acceptance threshold, so more tweaking there would waste budget. The open question is whether a learned combiner adds anything over the best early model. Here that means stacking, which can reweight models per class, for example on Papillary and Lepidic where the models differ. It would run on members built at the best-known regularisation: L2, PCA 64, C=1e-4, meta_weight 3. A moderate stack_C=0.1 lets the stacker learn per-class weights without collapsing to a uniform average.
EXPECTED: If per-class model complementarity is real, AUROC should reach about 0.888-0.892, with Papillary and Lepidic improving, and the gain over #10 should clear the threshold. If it lands at or below about 0.884, I will conclude that late stacking adds no signal beyond regularised early concatenation. I would then do at most one or two cheap early_tuned checks at C=1e-4 before accepting the plateau.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion with strong shrinkage (C=1e-4, L2, balanced blocks) is the best family at about 0.884. It is flat across PCA 64/128/None, meta_weight 3/10 and L2 on/off, with all differences well under 0.001. Late, stack, learned weights and gated fusion are clearly worse or no better. The clearest lever so far was C: moving from 1e-3 to 1e-4 added about 0.007 in early fusion.
REASONING: early_tuned was only tried at C=0.001, the setting that also underperformed in plain early fusion. Its learned per-block weights plus the members' own PCA/L2 could add a gain on top of the strong shrinkage that helped early fusion. Testing C=1e-4 answers whether the per-block weighting gives anything beyond plain early fusion. Further PCA or meta tweaks on #10 are clearly noise-level.
EXPECTED: I expect about 0.880-0.888. If it fails to beat #10 by the threshold, I conclude per-block weighting adds nothing and early fusion has plateaued. Then I would run one or two checks (e.g. balance_blocks=False at pca=None) and let the stop rule end the search.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion at the lowest C (0.0001) with per-model L2, block balancing and meta_weight 3 sits on a plateau of about 0.884-0.885 AUROC. That holds whether PCA is 64, 128 or off, with or without L2, and with meta_weight 3 or 10. All variants are within noise of #10, and early_tuned also converges there. Late fusion (mean_prob, stack) and gated fusion are clearly worse at matched settings, so strong shrinkage on a joint linear model is what works.
REASONING: One knob on the winning branch is untested: balance_blocks=False. Without PCA, Virchow2's 2560 columns would dominate the 1536-d blocks. This tells us whether equalising the blocks is actually needed or whether letting the strongest-dimensional embedding carry more weight helps under heavy shrinkage. It is a structurally different weighting rather than another near-duplicate PCA or meta tweak, so it has some chance of a real gain and is informative either way.
EXPECTED: Most likely a similar or slightly lower AUROC (about 0.880-0.885), which would confirm that block balancing is neutral-to-helpful and that the early-fusion plateau is the ceiling. A clear gain above threshold would mean the unbalanced block weighting is better. A clear drop (more than 0.005) would confirm that Virchow2 dominance hurts and that balancing is essential.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion at the strongest regularisation (C=1e-4, L2, balanced blocks) gives about 0.884-0.885. PCA 64/128/None, meta_weight 3 vs 10, L2 on/off, balance on/off and early_tuned all land inside ±0.001, which is noise. Late (stack, mean_prob) and gated are clearly worse. The response is driven by C, and C=1e-4 sits at the edge of the grid.
REASONING: C cannot go lower, so the remaining lever on effective capacity is fewer PCA components. The PCA curve has been mapped at 64, 128 and None, all flat, but never at 16 or 32 with C=1e-4. PCA=16 per model (48 image features in total) is the most aggressive dimension cut available. It tests whether even stronger implicit regularisation helps, which is the only direction the evidence supports.
EXPECTED: Most likely a result within ±0.003 of 0.8844 (not accepted), or a small drop if 16 components discard pattern-specific signal, e.g. for Papillary or Lepidic. If it is not clearly better, I conclude the early-fusion family has plateaued near 0.885, about +0.014 over the best single model, and spend the few remaining patience trials on untested corners (meta_weight=1) rather than fine-tuning.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion with strong shrinkage (C=1e-4) and L2 normalisation plateaus at about 0.884–0.885 AUROC regardless of PCA (64, 128 or none), meta_weight, block balancing or early_tuned. All of these give differences under 0.001, well below the threshold. Late fusion is consistently 0.005–0.02 worse, and stacking hurts. C sits at the edge of its grid, so further shrinkage in the linear-fusion family cannot be explored.
REASONING: The linear early-fusion family is saturated, and the remaining small knobs cannot clear the noise threshold. The one genuinely open direction is the gated method. Trial #4 (pca32, hidden32, wd0.1, 200 epochs) reached 0.8756 with the best balanced accuracy (0.511). Trial #16 (wd1.0, hidden16) fell to 0.859, which suggests heavy weight decay is not what limits it. Here I test whether early stopping helps: 100 epochs, strong input compression (PCA 16) and dropout 0.5, with lighter weight decay. A per-patient gate is the only fusion that could add something beyond a linear concatenation.
EXPECTED: If gating has real value, AUROC should approach or exceed 0.885 with lower fold SD than #4. If it lands at or below about 0.876, I conclude gated fusion offers no gain here. I would then spend the last trials on a confirmatory early variant rather than more gated tuning, and accept #10 as the final fusion.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion with very strong shrinkage (C=1e-4, L2 norm, balanced blocks) leads at about 0.884-0.885 AUROC. PCA dimension (64, 128 or none), balance_blocks and meta_weight 3 vs 10 make no detectable difference there, and the acceptance thresholds are only about 0.001-0.002. Late, stack, learned-weights and gated variants are all clearly worse. The fusion gain over the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870) is about +0.015, and this early-fusion plateau looks saturated.
REASONING: With 4 trials left before the stop rule, the remaining open question is whether early_tuned improves with more weight on metadata. Its member baselines favoured heavier meta weighting (H-optimus used 10), but early_tuned has only been tried at meta_weight 3. Its per-block inner-CV weights act as block-specific C values. Combined with stronger metadata weighting, this could help weak classes such as Papillary and Lepidic, where age and sex may carry signal. This is the only untested axis around the best C that has a plausible mechanism.
EXPECTED: AUROC about 0.884-0.888. If it is not accepted, I conclude that metadata weighting and per-block shrinkage are both exhausted near C=1e-4, and that early fusion at about 0.885 is the ceiling for linear fusion here. Trial #10 would remain the final choice.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion with strong shrinkage (C=1e-4, L2 norm, balanced blocks) leads at about 0.884-0.885 and is flat across PCA 64/128/None, block balancing and meta_weight 3 vs 10. Late, stacking, gated and tuned variants are consistently at or below this level; stacking and the gated network lose clearly. C is already at its grid minimum, so the main untested axis in the leading region is meta_weight=1.
REASONING: With 3 trials left before the stop rule, the most informative remaining knob in the best region is lower metadata weight. Trial #12 showed meta_weight=10 was slightly worse, so 1.0 completes that curve. I use pca=None, the numerically best variant (#13). The other untested options, late_tuned mean_logit and weighted_vote, belong to a method family that has trailed by about 0.005-0.015.
EXPECTED: AUROC about 0.884-0.886, most likely below the acceptance threshold. If it is not accepted, this confirms the early-fusion plateau is insensitive to all tunable knobs. In that case #10 (fusion, about +0.014 over the best single model, uni2h+meta) should stand as the final configuration rather than continuing to select on noise.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion with strong shrinkage (C=1e-4, L2 norm, balanced blocks) has plateaued at 0.884-0.886. PCA size, L2, meta_weight 3 vs 10 and balance_blocks barely matter there. Late, stack and gated variants are clearly worse, and stacking or gating overfits with 134 patients per fold. Every fusion near the plateau beats the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870) by about 0.015, but no change to the current best clears the noise threshold.
REASONING: Only 2 trials remain before the stop rule, so the most useful trial tests the one small lever that leaned positive: meta_weight=1, which gave +0.0011 in #23. Here I combine it with early_tuned, whose block weights are learned by inner CV and act as per-block shrinkage; that combination is untested. early_tuned with meta 3 and meta 10 sat at the plateau, and lower meta weight trended up. It is a cheap check of whether per-block regularisation plus less metadata emphasis gives a real paired gain.
EXPECTED: Likely about 0.884-0.886, below the acceptance threshold. If it is not accepted, I conclude the fusion optimum is the simple early concatenation with strong shrinkage (#10), at about +0.014 AUROC over the best single model. The remaining knob differences are noise.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion with strong shrinkage (C=1e-4, L2 norm, block balancing) has plateaued at 0.884-0.886. That is about 0.015 above the best single model (uni2h+meta, 0.870). PCA, meta_weight, balance_blocks and early_tuned all move AUROC by no more than 0.001, which is well below the acceptance thresholds. Gated, stacking and learned_weights are clearly worse, probably because 134 patients per fold are too few to fit the extra parameters.
REASONING: This is the last trial before the stop rule fires. Another early-fusion variant would only reshuffle knobs that are already flat, so it is noise-chasing. The one parameter-free combiner not yet tried with tuned members is late_tuned mean_logit. late_tuned mean_prob reached 0.879 with no fitted combination weights. A geometric mean sharpens agreement between members and could plausibly beat mean_prob by a few thousandths. It also answers the remaining open question about tuned late fusion.
EXPECTED: I expect about 0.878-0.884, i.e. not accepted over #10. If so, the search ends with early fusion #10 as the fusion choice: L2 norm, PCA 64, block balancing, C=1e-4, meta_weight 3. That would confirm the gain comes from heavily regularised joint fitting rather than the choice of combiner. A clear gain would instead indicate that member-specific tuning plus log-space averaging captures complementary errors better.
